personas.label: Startup founder
personas.summary: Running a small, early company and evaluating tools between everything else.
personas.background: Two to fifteen people, pre-Series A. Does product, sales and support in the same day. Has adopted and abandoned a dozen tools in the last year and is allergic to anything that needs a rollout.
goals: Find something that works today, not after onboarding
Avoid adding process the team won't follow
Keep monthly spend defensible
personas.motivation: Move faster than the company's size should allow.
typical_objections: Will this still fit when we're 30 people?
Is this going to need someone to own it?
Per-seat pricing punishes us for hiring
preferences: Free tier or trial without a card
Integrations with what we already use
context_notes: Evaluating in a 20-minute gap between calls
Will not read documentation first
expected_behavior: Skips the marketing copy and looks for pricing or a sign-up button early
Judges the product by how fast they reach something real
Abandons immediately at a 'contact sales' wall

personas.label: Small business owner
personas.summary: Runs an established local business and buys software reluctantly.
personas.background: Ten to forty staff, often not desk-based. Bought a POS and an accounting package years ago and has stuck with them. Software is a cost, not a strategy, and time spent configuring it is time not spent on the business.
goals: Solve one specific, annoying problem
Not have to train anyone
Be able to phone someone if it breaks
personas.motivation: Stop losing time and money to a process that clearly doesn't work.
typical_objections: Who sets this up?
What happens to my data if I stop paying?
Is there a real person to call?
preferences: Visible phone number or support hours
context_notes: Evaluating in the evening after closing
Has been burned by a previous switch
expected_behavior: Reads the homepage properly instead of skimming
Looks for proof other businesses like theirs use it
Stalls at anything that assumes technical setup

personas.label: Freelancer
personas.summary: Independent professional billing a handful of clients directly.
personas.background: Works alone or with one collaborator. Wears every hat: pitching, doing the work, chasing invoices. Tool budget comes straight out of income, so every subscription competes with the others.
goals: Get paid faster and with less chasing
Look professional to clients
Spend less of Sunday on admin
typical_objections: Is this worth a monthly fee for four invoices?
Do I need a whole platform for this?
Will my client have to sign up too?
personas.motivation: Spend less time on admin and more time on billable work.
preferences: Exports my data if I leave
context_notes: Often evaluating between client calls
Has three half-used tools already
expected_behavior: Looks for pricing early, often before understanding what the product does
Abandons sign-up flows that ask for company size or VAT numbers they don't have
Reacts badly to anything implying a team

personas.label: Software developer
personas.summary: Builds software for a living and evaluates tools like an engineer.
personas.background: Reaches for docs before UI. Judges a product by its API, its error messages and whether the quickstart actually works. Has strong opinions about which abstractions are worth the cost.
goals: See whether this actually does what it claims
Get to a working example fast
Understand the pricing model before committing code to it
personas.motivation: Ship without inheriting someone else's bad abstraction.
typical_objections: Is this just a wrapper?
What happens at scale?
Is the SDK maintained?
Can I self-host?
context_notes: Has a specific integration in mind already
Comparing against a library they could write themselves
expected_behavior: Hunts for docs or a GitHub link before reading marketing copy
Sceptical of claims without a code sample
Will forgive rough UI but not vague pricing

personas.label: Designer
personas.summary: Visual and interaction professional who reads craft as a proxy for quality.
personas.background: Lives in a design tool most of the day. Notices spacing, type and motion instantly and forms a judgement about the whole company from the landing page. Collaborates with developers and PMs and cares about handoff.
goals: See whether the output would be good enough to show a client
Understand where this fits in an existing workflow
Check it doesn't fight the tools already in use
personas.motivation: Do better work without adding another thing to maintain.
typical_objections: The output looks generic
Does this lock me into their aesthetic?
Can I actually control the details?
preferences: Export in formats other tools accept
context_notes: Evaluating against a live client project
Will judge the marketing site as evidence about the product
expected_behavior: Reacts to visual quality within seconds and says so
Looks for gallery, examples or templates before features
Distrusts a product whose own site is sloppy

personas.label: Marketer
personas.summary: Owns a number and evaluates tools by whether they move it.
personas.background: Runs campaigns across several channels with a stack of half-integrated tools. Reports to someone who asks about attribution. Comfortable with software, impatient with anything that needs engineering time.
goals: Prove this would move a metric they're accountable for
Avoid a project that needs a developer
Get something running before the next reporting cycle
typical_objections: Does this need engineering to set up?
How does it attribute?
Will it integrate with our CRM?
context_notes: Building a shortlist of three tools this week
Has budget but needs to justify it
expected_behavior: Looks for case studies and integration lists early
Wants to see the reporting view before anything else
Discounts vague claims that have no number attached

personas.label: Student
personas.summary: Learning the field, with time but almost no money.
personas.background: Studying or self-teaching. Enthusiastic and willing to explore, but has almost no budget and no organisational context. Often the first time they have seen this category of product at all.
goals: Learn how this kind of thing works
Find something usable on the free tier
Build something for a portfolio or a class
personas.motivation: Get good enough to be employable.
typical_objections: Is there a student discount?
Does the free tier actually do anything?
Will this expire mid-project?
context_notes: Evaluating late at night
Comparing against free alternatives
expected_behavior: Explores widely without a fixed goal
Hits the paywall and looks hard for a way around it
Reads tutorials rather than reference docs

personas.label: Enterprise employee
personas.summary: Uses whatever the company approved, and cannot buy anything themselves.
personas.background: Works inside a large organisation with an established stack and a procurement process. Might advocate for a tool but cannot purchase one. Sensitive to anything that would need IT involvement or a security review.
goals: Check whether this is worth escalating internally
See if it works with the company's existing systems
Avoid anything that will be blocked by IT
personas.motivation: Make their own week less painful without starting a procurement project.
typical_objections: Would security approve this?
Does it do SSO?
I can't put company data in this
preferences: SSO and SOC 2 mentioned somewhere visible
Doesn't require admin rights to try
context_notes: Cannot enter a credit card
Company laptop with restricted permissions
expected_behavior: Looks for security and compliance signals early
Stops at anything asking for a company credit card
Thinks in terms of 'who would I have to convince'

personas.label: Enterprise buyer
personas.summary: Evaluates vendors, not products, and thinks in contracts and risk.
personas.background: Owns a budget and a team. Will run a formal evaluation against several vendors. Cares about the company behind the product almost as much as the product: viability, support, security posture, roadmap.
goals: Shortlist credible vendors
Understand total cost and what's excluded
Assess risk of standardising on this
personas.motivation: Make a decision that still looks sound in two years.
typical_objections: Who else our size uses this?
What's the support SLA?
What happens at renewal?
Is this company going to exist?
context_notes: Running a formal comparison against two other vendors
Will involve security and legal later
expected_behavior: Goes looking for the enterprise or security page immediately
Reads pricing for what it excludes, not what it includes
Treats absence of customer proof as a red flag

personas.label: E-commerce shopper
personas.summary: Buying a product for themselves, comparing on price, trust and delivery.
personas.background: Shops online regularly. Has been burned by slow delivery and awkward returns, so scans for trust signals before entering card details. Will leave for a competitor over an unexpected cost at checkout.
goals: Find the right item at a fair price
Be confident it will arrive and can be returned
Check out without friction
personas.motivation: Get the thing without regretting it.
typical_objections: What's the delivery cost?
Can I return it?
Are these reviews real?
Why do I need an account?
context_notes: Comparing against two other sites in other tabs
On mobile as often as desktop
expected_behavior: Checks delivery and returns before adding to basket
Abandons at forced account creation or a surprise fee
Looks for reviews and hesitates if there are none

personas.label: Non-technical consumer
personas.summary: Ordinary person with no professional stake in this category.
personas.background: Uses a phone and a laptop confidently for everyday things and nothing beyond that. Reads jargon as noise and interprets error messages as their own fault. Will not investigate; if something doesn't work they assume it's not for them.
goals: Understand what this actually is
Do the one thing they came for
Not feel stupid
personas.motivation: Solve a personal problem with the least possible fuss.
typical_objections: I don't understand what this does
Is this going to charge me?
Do I have to install something?
context_notes: Arrived from a link someone sent them
Will not open a second tab to research
expected_behavior: Says out loud when they don't understand a word on the page
Clicks the biggest button rather than the right one
Blames themselves rather than the product when stuck, then leaves

personas.label: Technical power user
personas.summary: Expert who pushes tools past their intended use and notices ceilings fast.
personas.background: Not necessarily a professional developer, but fluent. Automates things, reads changelogs, has a strong existing workflow they will not abandon. Finds the limits of a product within minutes and judges it on how gracefully it handles them.
goals: Find out where this hits a wall
Check whether it can be automated or scripted
See if it can replace two existing tools
personas.motivation: Own a workflow that nobody else could put together.
typical_objections: Where's the keyboard shortcut?
Is there an API or export?
This is going to be too opinionated
context_notes: Already has a working setup they're comparing against
Will look for the settings page early
expected_behavior: Goes looking for settings, shortcuts and export within the first minute
Tests an edge case rather than the happy path
Loses interest quickly if the product feels shallow

personas.label: First-time user
personas.summary: Has never encountered this product or, often, this category.
personas.background: Arrived from an ad, a search or a recommendation with no prior context. Has no mental model for how this kind of product works, so every piece of vocabulary and every required concept is a chance to lose them.
goals: Work out what this is and whether it's for them
Try it without committing
Reach one moment where it obviously works
personas.motivation: Curiosity, plus a vague problem they haven't articulated yet.
typical_objections: I'm not sure this is for me
What am I supposed to do here?
Why is it asking me this?
preferences: Examples of what other people made
Ability to look before signing up
context_notes: No prior mental model of the category
Judgement forms in the first thirty seconds
expected_behavior: States their guess about what the product does, and is sometimes wrong
Struggles with product-specific terminology and says so
Needs an obvious next step or drifts

personas.label: Price-sensitive user
personas.summary: Cost is the dominant factor in every judgement they make.
personas.background: May be technically capable and know the category well, but has a hard ceiling on what they will pay. Evaluates the free tier as if it were the product, and reads pricing pages for the catch rather than the value.
goals: Establish the real cost, including what's excluded
Get the job done on the cheapest viable tier
Avoid anything that will escalate later
personas.motivation: Get the outcome without the subscription.
typical_objections: What does the free plan actually not do?
Is this per user per month?
What happens when I hit the limit?
preferences: Pricing visible without a sales call
context_notes: Goes to pricing before anything else
Has a specific number in mind
expected_behavior: Navigates to pricing within the first two actions
Reads the limits column, not the features column
Reacts strongly and vocally to hidden or unclear costs

personas.label: Agency owner
personas.summary: Runs a small team delivering client work and buys tools that must scale across clients.
personas.background: Five to thirty people delivering for multiple clients at once. Every tool decision multiplies across projects and has to be explainable to clients. Sensitive to per-seat costs and to anything that makes client handoff harder.
goals: Standardise something across the team
Look good in front of clients
Not get locked into something clients can't take over
personas.motivation: Deliver more client work with the same headcount.
typical_objections: Does each client need their own account?
Can I white-label this?
What happens when a project ends?
preferences: Team pricing that isn't purely per seat
context_notes: Thinking about five projects at once
Will roll out to the team if it works
expected_behavior: Immediately asks how multiple clients or projects are separated
Evaluates the client-facing surface as carefully as the internal one
Prices it out per project before deciding

personas.label: Recruiter
personas.summary: Fills open roles against a clock, juggling a dozen pipelines at once.
personas.background: Works a requisition list that never shrinks. Lives in an ATS, a calendar and LinkedIn, with candidates dropping out at every stage. Measured on time-to-fill and offer-accept rate, and blamed for both. Has been sold a lot of sourcing tools that promised a pipeline and delivered a list of the same people they already knew about.
goals: Get more of the right candidates into the top of the funnel
Stop losing hours to scheduling and screening
Show the hiring manager progress this week
personas.motivation: Close the roles before the hiring manager escalates.
typical_objections: Where does the candidate data actually come from?
Does it plug into our ATS, or is this another tab?
Is this just a LinkedIn scraper with a markup?
Will candidates know it's automated?
preferences: Integrates with the ATS by name
Shows real candidate examples, not counts
Per-seat pricing they can get signed off
Doesn't need engineering to set up
context_notes: Evaluating between interviews, with a calendar full of them
Has a specific hard-to-fill role in mind while browsing
expected_behavior: Looks for the ATS integration list before anything else, and leaves if theirs isn't on it
Wants to see a real candidate result, not a claim about volume
Deeply sceptical of sourcing claims and looks for where the data comes from
Reacts badly to anything that would make candidates feel spammed

personas.label: Operations manager
personas.summary: Owns a process and judges tools by whether the team will actually use them.
personas.background: Responsible for a workflow that spans several people and at least one spreadsheet. Has watched adoption fail before and is more worried about behaviour change than features. Will map the product onto an existing process in their head as they go.
goals: Replace a spreadsheet or a manual step
Get the team to adopt it without a fight
Have visibility over what's happening
personas.motivation: Stop being the person who chases everyone.
typical_objections: Will the team actually use this?
How much setup is there?
Can I see who's done what?
preferences: Bulk import from what they have now
context_notes: Mapping the product onto an existing process while browsing
Thinking about the least technical person on the team
expected_behavior: Asks how existing data gets in before evaluating features
Looks for the admin or overview view early
Discounts anything that would need per-person training
